📸 Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro — Xalapa, Veracruz · 6 de junio de 2026

🇲🇽✊ "For years, being young in Mexico meant being a suspect. If you didn't study, you were a vagrant." Subsecretary of Employment Quiahuitl Chávez at today's Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro assembly in Xalapa. Under the neoliberal model an entire generation was criminalized in the press as "ninis" and abandoned by the state. The 4T flipped the framing: young people aren't a problem to manage — they're citizens with rights to work, healthcare, and education. 3.5 million have entered the program since 2018. — Quiahuitl Chávez Domínguez, Subsecretaria de Empleo

🇲🇽✊ "For 36 years the neoliberal model was imposed on Mexico. And the people suffered." Sheinbaum drew the line from 1982 to today: nearly four decades of austerity, privatization, and a generation of young people stigmatized as "ninis" — when the actual failure was a state that refused to invest in them. "It's not the young person's fault. It's the fault of a government that didn't generate the conditions." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Xalapa, Veracruz

🇲🇽✊ "Access to education is a right. Access to healthcare is a right. Access to dignified work is a right." Since 2018, 3.5 million young Mexicans have entered the workforce through Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro — monthly minimum wage plus IMSS health coverage, one full year of paid work experience. Total public investment: over 170 billion pesos in 7.5 years. Neoliberalism called this impossible. The 4T calls it a right. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Xalapa, Veracruz

🇲🇽🌎 "Imagine letting Mexico be governed from abroad. No. Independence cost us too much." Sheinbaum tied today's local infrastructure announcement directly to the question of who runs Mexico. The line came at the inauguration of flood-protection works for five communities along the Bobos River — 10 kilometers of embankment, 700 million pesos, planned and built with Mexican resources. Governor Rocío Nahle: "It is an honor to walk hand in hand with the first woman President. But what a first woman President." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Carrillo Puerto, Veracruz

🇲🇽✊ "What did the governments before López Obrador do? Nothing." For decades, neoliberal governments left Veracruz communities to flood every rainy season. Today Sheinbaum inaugurated a 10 km flood protection embankment along the Bobos River — a 700 million peso investment shielding five communities: La Reforma, La Constancia, Troncones, La Defensa, Felipe Carrillo Puerto. In the past year alone, CONAGUA built 1,117 water infrastructure works across 140 municipalities in Veracruz. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Carrillo Puerto, Veracruz

🇲🇽🐉🌐 HIDALGO OPENS DOORS AS WASHINGTON DEMANDS THEY CLOSE

While the U.S. pressures Mexico City to wall off Chinese capital, the state of Hidalgo is doing the opposite. State officials confirmed this week they are deepening talks with a Chinese delegation focused on strategic investment, technology transfer, and direct exports to Asian markets.

Hidalgo has already pulled in MX$117 billion (US$6.8 billion) in private investment across 104 active projects, with 157,600 jobs in the pipeline. In February, the state joined CDMX and the State of Mexico to launch the Central Mexico Economic Zone, pooling infrastructure and capital strategy across the country's industrial core.

This is what diversification looks like on the ground: states multiplying options instead of waiting for federal permission. China is one node in a multipolar map — not a binary choice.

🇲🇽🐉🔥 EBRARD TO WASHINGTON: "RETURN TO FREE TRADE"

Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard confirmed Mexico will demand the elimination of U.S. tariffs at the second USMCA negotiating round on June 16-17 in Washington. The optimal outcome, he told reporters this week: "a return to free trade."

Washington wants harder rules of origin to block Chinese content from North American supply chains — a unilateral demand that would lock Mexico into one trading bloc and away from Asian diversification. Ebrard called out the new U.S. logic: a system "in which different parties will be charged different tariffs," a sharp break from the 1994 framework Mexico signed in good faith.

A third round in Mexico City is set for the week of July 20. Sovereignty means trading on Mexico's terms — not Washington's.
